title: The Agent Token Primitive is marked Active while the token's address, admin and distribution process are all undefined
content:
Obex's Agent Token Primitive carries Global Activation Status `Active` (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.4.1.1) and its Instance Configuration Document sits under Active Instances. Yet within that document: "The address of OBEX will be specified in a future iteration of the Obex Artifact" (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.4.2.1.1.4), "The token Admin will be specified in a future iteration" (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.4.2.1.1.5), and the Operational Process Definition for "minting and initial distribution of the tokens from the Genesis Supply" states these "will be defined in a future iteration" (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.4.2.1.2). The Agent's Genesis Account is likewise deferred (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.1.3.1.1.4).

What *is* fixed is the economically binding part: name, symbol OBEX, a Genesis Supply of 10 billion, and the permanent emissions disablement. What is deferred is everything about who controls the token and how it reaches holders.

The tension is with `Active` as a status. Elsewhere in the Atlas, `Active` marks a Primitive that is operating; here it marks one whose deployed artifact does not yet have an address. Either `Active` means "Invoked and irrevocably committed" rather than "live on chain," or the status is running ahead of reality.

The ordering is nonetheless defensible and possibly deliberate: supply and emission rules are hardest to change credibly after launch, so fixing them first and leaving mechanics open costs less than the reverse. The disclosure is uniform and explicit rather than hidden, which keeps the gap auditable.
description: Obex's Instance sits under Active Instances with a named token, symbol and 10-billion Genesis Supply, but three fields defer to "a future iteration of the Obex Artifact".
